sampleClock: Date.now() at entry to EACH liveSample(), before log and workload IO
factType: explicit observed safe integer wall-clock milliseconds; never inferred from raw.now or a wait constant
precision: Date.now integer milliseconds; ISO serialization by Date.toISOString(); event parsing exactly existing Date.parse(), no new rounding
logQuery: kubectl logs --since-time=<start ISO> --tail=1000; then existing runtimeWindow performs both bounds locally
historicalQuery: baseline --since=10m; final --since-time=baseline.capturedAt; --tail=500; diagnostics only, no Loki Gate query
wait: setTimeout(16000) only if first window has candidate count>=2; a requested wait, not an authoritative timestamp or maximum interval
interval: t2 = Date.now at second sample. Under an unadjusted clock, t2-t1 includes first log IO, parse work, workload IO, timer wait and timer scheduling latency
secondQueryLatency: occurs after t2 capture; does not advance that query's end bound
firstQueryLatency: occurs after t1 capture; contributes to t2 but does not move the first end bound
preSamplingLatency: diagnostic and earlier IO can move first sample time away from raw.now; sample0 also requires an observed timestamp
retry: none in frozen run() or health fetch; failed command terminates Gate path
commandTimeout: kubectl --request-timeout=15s; spawnSync timeout=20000; nonzero/null status fails with no retry
wallClockAdjustment: not assumed monotonic; consume actual clock values and retain original persistentRuntime disjoint-window rejection
modeScope: baseline and check use the identical liveSample/wait code; baseline establishment and final continuity validation differ and remain unchanged
missingTiming: incomplete evidence, NOT_CONFIGURED/null decision if the successful sample's observed clock is absent or malformed; never synthesize fixed offset or PASS
rawFactPreservation: input evidence, event timestamps and query outcomes unchanged; only adapter consumes the previously missing explicit per-sample clock
